bugs.description: table() averages each row over 'valid sources only' and then over whatever pairs still have valid states, but the tables are titled 'Mean over the 8 pairs'. Rows therefore rest on different pairs and sources and are not comparable with each other; 'sae5' silently disappears. The same holds for contrast() (line 83), which prints e.g. '(3/3 pairs)'.
bugs.evidence: Valid share per pair (replicated, identical invalid counts to mim_attack_t0.log): sae5 0/236 states; sae20 24/236 (pair 0: 8 sources, pair 3: 1 source, pair 5: 15 sources; distance 3.2-5.9 x t0); lens_lvlstar only pairs 2,3,5,6,7; laminf_lvlstar pair 4 59% (path end score 1.425 vs s* 1.420, so validity is decided by where the step overshoots); doseinf_1.5 pair 7 0%; doseinf_2 pair 7 0%, pair 4 34%, pair 6 62%. Consequence in the official log: table A row sae20 shows dR 1.79 (largest value in the table) and section F prints 'sae20 minus lam0_lvlstar: output +1.66 [+1.41,+1.93] (3/3 pairs)' - 24 states, one pair represented by a single source, pair 0 with a real gap of 0.70 [0.04,1.42]. Dose table E: mean dR 0.41 -> 0.58 from dose 1 to 1.5 as tabulated, 0.31 -> 0.58 on the pairs present at every dose (pair 7, dR 1.12, drops out).
bugs.fix: Print n_pairs and n_states per row; compute every table and contrast on the common support of the rows being compared (same pairs, same sources); add intention-to-treat rows that keep the saved end state when a level is not reached; suppress rows below a coverage threshold (e.g. <80% of sources in every pair).

bugs.description: The SAE-feature-only displacement matched on probe score (sae5 / sae20, valid only if the coefficient c <= 3) does not exist for almost all sources, so the intended control 'interpretable units at the same probe score' is effectively absent, while its few surviving states enter table A and contrast F.
bugs.evidence: mim_attack_t0.log: invalid sae5 236 of 236, sae20 212 of 236. The 24 surviving sae20 states are 3.2-5.9 x t0 away from the source and give dR 2.47 (pair 0), 0.69 (pair 3, n=1), 2.20 (pair 5).
bugs.fix: Drop sae5/sae20 from tables and contrasts. If an SAE displacement is wanted, define it without reference to the probe: project the class-mean difference on the span of the selected decoder directions (SAE-visible part) and patch that part and the remainder separately, matched on class-mean coordinate or on distance; keep sae20_c1 as the natural-dose variant.

bugs.description: dR = (r_patched - r_source) / gap divides by the real held-out gap (line 30) without any check that the gap is reliably different from zero, and the per-pair ratios are then averaged with equal weight.
bugs.evidence: Recomputed on real prompts (chk6, chk10): gap 0.70 [0.04,1.42], 0.85 [0.19,1.60], 0.64 [0.06,1.31] for pairs 0-2 against 2.03, 7.17, 2.35, 7.10, 22.17 for pairs 3-7 (35-fold range); AUROC of the output score on real held-out prompts 0.82/0.78/0.65 for pairs 0-2; official log: KL real A->A (6.57, 8.85) is larger than KL real A->B (4.78, 8.11) for pairs 0 and 2. Source-level SD of dR for the probe-normal state is 0.59/0.69/1.15 in pairs 0-2 against 0.12-0.38 in pairs 3-7. With the denominator resampled the interval of dR(lam0_lvlstar) is [-0.08,+6.0], [+0.28,+3.7], [+0.20,+108] for pairs 0-2. saerec (state replaced by its SAE reconstruction) gets dR 1.22 in pair 2.
bugs.fix: Gate pairs on a pre-specified reliability criterion (e.g. AUROC of r on real held-out prompts >= 0.9 and gap interval clearly excluding 0), propagate the denominator into the intervals, and report next to dR a measure that needs no ratio: the share of patched outputs above the 95th percentile of real A (fixed false-positive rate, as Biggio's FN at fixed FP) and the shift in pooled SDs of r. Report per pair; do not average ratios over pairs with unreliable denominators.

bugs.description: The density percentile of a swapped-in real B state is computed against all reference states including itself (self-kernel 1), while the reference distribution lpB is leave-one-out. The real-B reference row 'swap' is therefore biased upward.
bugs.evidence: Official table A: swap dens_pct 0.57; exchangeable real held-out B states have 0.48 leave-one-out. Replication with self-inclusion: 0.55-0.60 in every pair.
bugs.fix: For swap variants take the leave-one-out value of the swapped state (lpB[k]) instead of evaluating it against the full reference set.

bugs.description: The 10-nearest-neighbour vote counts the surrogate's own training states S1 (the attractors of the density term and of the centroid) as neighbours, and the isolation ratio divides by one global median nearest-neighbour distance although that distance differs strongly between families.
bugs.evidence: Real held-out B states: nnB 0.68 (0.49-0.84 by pair), 0.60 when S1 is excluded; centroid-like states 0.94-0.96, i.e. above real B. Median nearest-neighbour distance by family 271 (incorrect_answer) to 422 (threatening_user) against NN0 = 361, so unmodified real states already have iso 0.78-1.21 depending on the family.
bugs.fix: Restrict neighbour candidates to states not used to build the attack (S2, test prompts, other families); compare with the value real held-out B states obtain rather than with 1; normalise isolation by the family-specific nearest-neighbour distance and read it two-sided.

bugs.description: split3 seeds the generator with 1000 + seed for every pair, so pairs that share a family of the same size get identical splits of that family. The '8 pairs' are then treated as independent in contrast().
bugs.evidence: At seed 0: pairs 0 and 3 use the same 31 source prompts (205 unique sources for 236 source rows); pairs 4 and 5 use the same 38 real-B reference prompts and the same B training states (identical h = 789.6). For the shared sources the raw output-score change of the probe-normal state correlates 0.81 between pair 0 and pair 3.
bugs.fix: Seed the split with a hash of (a, b, seed), or keep the shared splits and resample shared prompts jointly; in either case treat pairs sharing a family as one cluster in the uncertainty.

bugs.description: The level 'lvlstar' (median probe score of real unseen B) is not below 'lvlone' (training margin, score 1) in most pairs, so tables B (score 0), A (s*), C (score 1) are not an ordered dose series although their titles suggest it.
bugs.evidence: s* = 0.83, 1.27, 0.82, 1.13, 1.42, 1.16, 1.30, 1.03: above 1 in 6 of 8 pairs. Official tables: lam0_lvlone distance 0.96 x t0, below lam0_lvlstar (1.00).
bugs.fix: State s* per pair next to the tables, or define the levels as quantiles of the held-out B score distribution (e.g. 10th, 50th, 90th percentile).

bugs.description: The within-family KL reference draws both prompts independently, so a prompt can be paired with itself (KL 0).
bugs.evidence: Code reading: zip(rng.choice(teA, 60), rng.permutation(rng.choice(teA, 60))); probability of a self-pair 1/|teA|, about 3%, i.e. a downward bias of klAA of about 3% - negligible next to the other issues.

design_issues.issue: Matching: 'equal probe score' is not 'equal B content'. The headline comparison (probe normal vs class-mean translation at the same surrogate score s*) has three different answers depending on what is matched, and the only matching that isolates the probe-specific direction shows no difference.
design_issues.why: At s* the probe-normal state has moved 0.44 of the class-mean difference (0.13-0.82 by pair), the class-mean translation 0.91 (0.78-1.03), and it is 1.56 x farther away. Patched results (recomputed, identical to the official table A values): dR 0.38 vs 0.90 at equal probe score (ratio 0.42; official contrast +0.52 [0.43,0.63], 8/8); 0.38 vs 0.53 at equal distance (ratio 0.71, difference -0.15 [-0.22,-0.09]); 0.38 vs 0.36 at equal class-mean coordinate (ratio 1.06, difference +0.02 [-0.04,+0.07], per pair -0.23..+0.18). The last holds at every dose of the probe-normal line (0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 x t0: differences -0.02, -0.02, +0.02, -0.02, -0.06; for dR2 at most 0.013). So the output reaction to a probe-normal move is exactly what its class-mean component predicts; the rest of the probe normal is causally inert. Statement I of the log ('output moved less than a quarter of the real gap for 0.60 of the probe-normal states') is equally true of class-mean translations with the same class-mean coordinate (0.61). Conversely the probe normal is far from ineffective: +0.36 over a random-label normal of the same length (8/8 pairs). Within a pair, across all variant types, the class-mean coordinate predicts dR better (Spearman 0.70-0.96) than the probe score (0.59-0.83) or the distance (0.67-0.84). Caveats of this check: linear interpolation on a three-point class-mean line, one split.
design_issues.suggestion: Report all three matchings side by side and make headline claims only for comparisons that survive them. Replace the lambda family by an explicit factorial of displacement components: a x (class-mean difference), b x (probe normal orthogonalised against the class-mean difference), c x (deletion of the prompt's own deviation from its family centroid), each as a dose series. Add the two decisive variants: (i) a pure probe-specific move, x0 + t*w_perp, which brings the surrogate to s* at about 1.35 x t0 with class-mean coordinate 0 (prediction from the present data: probe says typical B, network does not react); (ii) a probe-blind move, x0 + c*(dm - (dm.w_hat) w_hat), which changes the class-mean coordinate while the surrogate score stays at the source value. Together they are the double dissociation the question asks for.

design_issues.issue: 'The probe' is not unique: the hard-margin SVM normal is one of many equally accurate readouts, and the result is specific to it.
design_issues.why: On the same S1 data (mean over the 8 pairs): hard-margin SVM AUROC 0.990, cosine with the class-mean difference 0.67; SVM with C=1 AUROC 0.984, cosine 0.95 (its 'attack to s*' is essentially a class-mean translation, class-mean coordinate 0.88 instead of 0.44); class-mean probe AUROC 0.981; LDA with pooled within-family covariance accuracy 0.96, cosine 0.52 with the hard-margin normal and 0.44 with the mean difference. Surrogate normals of the same pair from different splits have cosine 0.51-0.74 (0.93 only for pair 7). The same probe-normal states at s* are 'read as B' by 99% (LDA), 57% (independent hard-margin probe), 30% (nearest centroid on the raw state), 29% (SAE nearest centroid). The part of the probe normal orthogonal to the mean difference behaves as a suppressor in the sense of filter-vs-pattern (Haufe et al.): within a family, real held-out prompts further along it have less B-like output (Spearman -0.28 [-0.42,-0.11]), while the class-mean coordinate is positively related (+0.44 [0.33,0.54]) and the probe coordinate as a whole +0.36 [0.29,0.43].
design_issues.suggestion: Either state every conclusion for 'the max-margin normal of a hard-margin SVM fitted on about 55 states in 2048 dimensions', or repeat the closed-form attack for at least three probe families (class-mean difference, regularised SVM/logistic with cross-validated C, LDA with pooled covariance) and report how the reaction at s* changes with the regulariser. Describe the finding as 'the probe score overstates the B content of a minimum-norm move by about a factor of two', not as 'probe separability does not show what the network uses'.

design_issues.issue: 'Pure mimicry' with bandwidth = median pairwise distance is translation to the B centroid; large-lambda states are prototypes, not states from the dense region of real B.
design_issues.why: Kernel weights at a source are uniform (effective number of weights 25.4-33.2 of 26-34 points); cosine between the density gradient and the direction to the centroid 0.999 (minimum 0.997); the path is straight (0.98-1.00) and ends 7-36 units from the centroid (0.02-0.07 of the within-family radius), while real held-out B states sit 350-540 from the centroid and none is closer than 226. The density is nearly flat (end/source ratio 1.3-2.5). There is no usable bandwidth: the leave-one-out likelihood optimum is 1.5% of the median distance (h about 7-12), where one neighbour has all the weight; between 0.1 and 0.5 of the median distance the estimate flips from nearest neighbour to centroid. At s*, lambda=1/5/inf states are 42%/73%/93% of the way to the centroid; lambda=5 and inf states have a norm below 97% of all real states and are flagged as atypical by a two-sided typicality test in 99%/100% of cases (real held-out B 6%). In pairs 0-3 only 32-43% of the squared centroid move is along the class difference; the rest deletes the prompt's own content (norm 283-449, i.e. 0.3-1.5 x the centroid distance). Network: centroid dR 1.13 and lambda=inf 1.08 exceed the class-mean translation (0.90) and, in pairs 3-7, the real swap (1.30 vs 1.11) - a prototype super-stimulus, not 'more B-like'. Lambda itself is implemented faithfully (gradient ratio changes by at most 12% along a path), so every finite lambda is a fixed blend of two straight directions.
design_issues.suggestion: Rename the lambda=inf variants ('centroid replacement / prototype') and describe large-lambda results as 'class-mean translation plus removal of the prompt-specific component'; never as on-distribution or realistic B states. If a mimicry arm is wanted, use the transport that preserves typicality: under a shared-covariance model this is the class-mean translation itself (full dose x0 + muB - muA, not yet patched), with family-specific shrunk covariances the Gaussian optimal-transport map; the other end is interpolation towards the nearest real B state. Patch the pure content-deletion variant (x0 -> muA) to separate that effect.

design_issues.issue: The output measure (expected log-likelihood ratio of the first response token) is not valid for 3 of the 8 pairs, and the 8-pair mean of dR mixes scales.
design_issues.why: Pairs 0-2 (ai_accelerationism <-> pro_trisolarans in both directions, climate_denial -> flat_earth): the first token is 'The' in both families (0.69 vs 0.55; 0.46 vs 0.26); total variation between the class-mean distributions 0.22-0.36 against a within-family split-half floor of 0.20-0.43; AUROC 0.82/0.78/0.65; power to detect a REAL held-out B prompt at 5% false positives 0.53/0.10/0.16; the lens reproduces -0.26 and -0.18 of the gap in pairs 0 and 2 (wrong sign). Yet these pairs contribute the largest dR of the probe-normal state after pair 7 (0.61, 0.63) although its calibrated evasion there is at baseline (0.04 vs 0.04; 0.20 vs 0.08). Pair 7 is the opposite extreme: t0 is 0.90 of the centroid distance and 78% of the state norm, the probe normal is almost the mean difference (cosine 0.91), dR 0.98. The '0.38' in table A is therefore an average of 0.03-0.31 in the four informative pairs (3-6: 0.06, 0.24, 0.03, 0.31), two noise-dominated values and one trivial one.
design_issues.suggestion: Pre-specify a validity gate for the output measure and report pairs that fail it separately (here pairs 0-2 fail). Report per pair with intervals that include the denominator; use the calibrated evasion rate (pairs 3-7: probe normal 0.06/0.03/0.07/0.31/1.00, class-mean translation 0.42/0.93/0.29/0.81/1.00, swap 0.71/0.86/0.70/0.88/1.00, real B 0.67/0.90/0.53/0.84/1.00) as the primary outcome. For families that do not differ in the first token, measure later: generate 16-32 tokens for a reduced variant set and score them with an A-vs-B text classifier.

design_issues.issue: The second reaction measure (projection of the final state on the class-mean difference, dR2) contains a direct copy of the patched displacement through the residual connection.
design_issues.why: The dR2 read-out direction applied directly to the unprocessed block-21 states separates real held-out prompts as well as the final states do (AUROC 0.92-1.00 vs 0.93-1.00); within a family the block-21 class-mean coordinate predicts the final-state projection with Spearman 0.88 [0.84,0.91]. With the pass-through gain calibrated on the random-direction controls (1/gain 34-44, consistent with the lens estimate 38 of the pre-norm RMS), the direct term accounts for 32-42% of the measured dR2 of every class-related variant (probe normal 0.38, class-mean translation 0.36, swap 0.35), 67% for lens_lvlstar and 72% for saerec. dR2 and the output measure can disagree in sign: the lens direction, built to maximise this projection, has dR2 +0.29 above the probe normal at equal distance but an output reaction 0.11 below it (official contrast F). Its AUROC of 0.99 in pairs where the output cannot tell the families apart shows it reads information that is not expressed in likely tokens.
design_issues.suggestion: Store the RMS of the pre-norm final state in mim_patch.py (tail() returns only the normalised state) and report dR2 net of the direct term g*delta/rms, or both; treat dR2 as secondary and never as 'the network's reaction' on its own. A read-out at the next generated position removes the direct path altogether.

design_issues.issue: 'The SAE reads B' (cosine nearest centroid on SAE activations) is not a statement about interpretable units, and the SAE is too lossy at this position for negative conclusions.
design_issues.why: The identical nearest-centroid rule on the raw state, fitted on the same prompts, gives the same answer for the probe-normal states at s*: SAE 0.29 vs raw 0.31 (per pair 0.35/0.39, 0.32/0.36, 0.20/0.24, 0.23/0.19, 0.07/0.07, 0.11/0.07, 0.03/0.12, 1.00/1.00); for the class-mean translation 0.90 vs 0.98. The gap between 'probe 1.00' and 'SAE 0.30' is the difference between a max-margin and a centroid classifier (LDA on the raw state says 0.99) plus more training data (60% of prompts vs 35%). The summary is also rule-dependent: a standardised rule on the same activations gives 0.66 instead of 0.07 in pair 4; 10-45% of the centroid difference sits on the 24 dense features. Each readout is fooled by the displacement built against it: sae20_c1 flips the SAE rule in 62% but the raw rule in 6% and the independent probe in 11%. SAE validity here: reconstruction error norm 444 vs a probe-normal displacement of 307; the change of the reconstruction captures 8% of the probe-normal displacement, 33% of the class-mean translation, 52% of real B-minus-A differences; a random direction of the same length switches 84 features (probe normal 47); replacing the state by its reconstruction changes the top-1 token in 24% of prompts (random direction 11-13%, 62% in pair 4); the SAE error term separates the 18 families as well as the reconstruction (0.864 vs 0.834).
design_issues.suggestion: Always print the same rule on the raw state next to the SAE reading and use a continuous, gap-normalised coordinate instead of a binary flip. Licensed: descriptive, feature-level, positive statements with the random-direction control (held-out validated discriminating features go from 0.29/0.80 on/off at the source to 0.60/0.55 under the probe-normal move, real B 0.80/0.32; unchanged under random directions), and causal statements from feature displacements that keep the error term (sae20_c1: dR 0.35 over 8 pairs, 0.21 over pairs 3-7, with the probes still reading A). Not licensed: 'the SAE is more robust than the probe', 'no B features, hence no B information', anything from saerec-type substitutions. For the question whether the units carry what the network uses, patch the SAE-visible and SAE-invisible parts of the class-mean difference separately. The lens-word labels (e.g. feature 13493 'arom, spice, secondary' with AUROC 1.00 for incorrect_answer) are not validated concept labels.

design_issues.issue: Density percentile, 10-nearest-neighbour vote and isolation ratio do not measure 'this looks like a real B state' in 2048 dimensions with about 30 reference points.
design_issues.why: Density percentile among real held-out B: real held-out A states get 0.20 on average (0.10-0.35 in seven pairs), real B 0.48, the probe-normal state 0.37, lambda=5 and the centroid 1.00 - it cannot tell A from B and gives the maximum to states no real B state resembles (the centroid is closer to every B state than any two B states are to each other). Neighbour vote: real held-out B 0.68, centroid-like states 0.94-0.96 (hubs). Isolation: real states 0.78-1.21 by family, centroid 0.88, so collapse cannot be flagged. Tested replacement: a two-sided Mahalanobis typicality under the pooled within-family covariance of all 18 families (100 principal directions plus isotropic tail), calibrated on held-out real B, flags real B 6%, real swap 4%, class-mean translation 10%, probe normal at s* 3%, 2 x t0 20%, random direction 24%, lambda=1 53%, lambda=5 99%, centroid 100%, lens_lvlstar 95% - but it does not separate real A from real B either (15% flagged). Any omnibus density is dominated by the roughly 1,900 class-irrelevant dimensions.
design_issues.suggestion: Report two separate things: (1) side - a cross-validated discriminative coordinate with held-out calibration (LDA: real A 5%, real B 96% on the B side); (2) typicality - two-sided percentiles of Mahalanobis statistic, state norm and distance to the family centroid among held-out real states, as share flagged at 5%. Optionally a cross-validated real-vs-variant discriminator (AUROC 0.5 = indistinguishable; not tested here). Drop dens_pct, or keep it only with the real-A reference row beside it.

design_issues.issue: Uncertainty: one split, 8 hand-picked and overlapping pairs, bootstrap over sources only.
design_issues.why: The intervals in section F condition on the 8 pair instances, the split, the fitted probes and the reference sets. Where it can be checked without the network, the split dominates: the share of probe-normal states the independent probe reads as B is 0.57 at seed 0, but over 10 splits the 8-pair mean has SD 0.102 against a pooled source-bootstrap SE of 0.030 (per pair SD up to 0.34, range 0.03-0.97 in pair 4). With pairs as units the intervals are: dR of the probe normal 0.38 [0.09,0.66] (script: [0.31,0.45]); class-mean translation minus probe normal 0.52 [0.28,0.76] (script: [0.43,0.63]); probe normal minus random-label normal 0.36 [0.09,0.63] (script: [0.29,0.43]), and inside pairs 3 and 5 that last contrast does not exclude 0 ([-0.02,0.13], [-0.01,0.10]). The pairs are neither representative nor independent: 7 of 153 family pairs, 11 of 18 families; four of the seven are in the bottom 8% of all pairs for probe accuracy and bottom 15% for SAE-feature separability; pairs {0,1,3,6}, {4,5}, {2}, {7} form four connected clusters through shared families, so '8/8 pairs' is at most four independent signs (two-sided sign test p = 0.125). Section F has 12 contrasts x 2 measures and no primary endpoint.
design_issues.suggestion: Licensed now: conditional statements about these 8 instances and the direction of large effects. Before quoting intervals: at least 5 split seeds (the tail-only patch needs about 8 minutes for 8.7k states; a reduced set of about 12 variants makes 5 seeds cheaper than the present run), a random or stratified sample of pairs (the model-free part can cover all 153), a hierarchical bootstrap or mixed model over seed, family cluster and source, two or three pre-specified primary contrasts with Holm correction, everything else labelled exploratory, and a per-pair forest plot instead of sign counts.

design_issues.issue: Conditioning on 'valid' states and on sources the surrogate reads as A.
design_issues.why: Validity selects in different directions: sae20 keeps sources where a 3-6 x t0 feature displacement happens to align with the probe (inflates dR); lens_lvlstar keeps the pairs where lens and probe are more aligned; high doses on the mimicry path lose the pair with the largest reaction (deflates the curve); laminf_lvlstar in pair 4 is decided by step overshoot. Restricting sources to surrogate score < 0 drops 14 real A prompts in pairs 1, 2, 4, 5 (9 more by the cap of 32). The effect on dR is small (within-source differences), but those prompts are the d_max = 0 point of Biggio's curve: in the two pairs with a reliable output measure their output is already shifted towards B by 0.38 and 0.25 of the gap (n = 3 and 4), and real B prompts read as A are shifted 0.65-0.80 towards A (n = 5 and 2).
design_issues.suggestion: Use common-support comparisons (see the table() bug), report validity as an outcome, and analyse the surrogate's natural errors on real held-out prompts as a separate stratum rather than excluding them.

design_issues.issue: What the first-token measures and the swap reference can and cannot show.
design_issues.why: 3-10 tokens carry 90% of the gap ('The', 'This', 'That', 'I', 'Sure', 'It', 'If', 'Let', 'We'): the measure captures the opener style that goes with a prompt type, not the content of a B-typical answer. For this measure the full swap is a proper ceiling: dR 1.11 (0.94-1.37 by pair), dR2 1.01, so attention of blocks 22-27 to the A prompt does not pull the first token back. That is established only for the first token; later positions read the A prompt directly. The swap also changes prompt-specific content (KL 9.0, top-1 changed in 78%) and there is no within-family swap to calibrate KL and top-1 change; values above 1 (centroid) are not 'more B'.
design_issues.suggestion: State the claim as 'first response token'. Add a within-family swap (real A state from another A prompt) as the null for KL/top-1 and report reactions relative to the swap of the same pair. Use a multi-token outcome before saying the network 'treats the state as B'.

design_issues.issue: Fidelity of the transfer from Biggio et al.: what carries over and where it breaks.
design_issues.why: Carried over correctly: objective and signs (maximise s + lambda*p is the mirror image of minimising g - lambda*p), unit-norm steps on the combined gradient, lambda scaled to the gradient sizes. Breaks: (1) the target is not a classifier - the network has no A/B decision at block 21, so 'evasion' has no success criterion and a graded, normalised reaction replaces FN at fixed FP; (2) Biggio's surrogate is trained to imitate the target, here it is trained on family labels the network was never asked about, so the experiment tests whether the output depends on the probe's direction, not transferability; (3) Biggio's targeted classifier has more data than the surrogate, here the independent probe has less (25% vs 35%) and is an equally unstable hard-margin fit, so transfer to it (0.57, SD 0.10 over splits) mostly measures the instability of such normals; (4) the density term degenerates (Biggio: Laplacian kernel, small h, 50 neighbours, about 100 dimensions, 500 samples); for a linear surrogate mimicry is not needed to cross the boundary and Biggio themselves find it only lengthens the path; (5) no d_max: paths are read at score levels, distance series exist only for lambda 0 and inf; (6) attack states have no pre-image (no prompt produces them), which Biggio treat as a limitation and which makes typicality diagnostics essential.
design_issues.suggestion: Present the result in Biggio's own format: evasion rate against distance (in units of the centroid distance) for each direction, for three targets - surrogate (perfect knowledge), independent probe (limited knowledge), network output at a fixed 5% false-positive rate - on a (direction x distance) grid from which equal-score, equal-distance and equal-class-mean comparisons can all be read.

design_issues.issue: Scope: prompt families of the base model are not DSSE side effects.
design_issues.why: No fine-tuned model is involved. The classes are sets of eval prompts that differ in topic, tone and format (e.g. capital letters in acting_distressed, word problems in incorrect_answer); a hard-margin probe separates almost any two of them (0.989 mean accuracy over 153 pairs, random-label test accuracy 0.509), which says nothing about a disposition acquired by fine-tuning. The base model shows the behaviours only at base rate. What may be claimed: methodological facts about this model at this site (first-token output follows the class-mean coordinate of an intervention; a max-margin probe score overstates it; the public SAE keeps about half of the between-prompt variance at the template position, 0.56/0.49 vs 0.81 on content tokens, and its readings are equivalent to a centroid readout of the raw state). Nothing may be claimed about how side effects are represented, detected or removed.
design_issues.suggestion: Fine-tune version: (1) class = model (fine-tuned on a DSSE dataset vs base, plus the random-data fine-tunes as null) on the SAME prompts, so prompt content cancels in paired differences; (2) unit of replication = dataset/fine-tune, with held-out datasets of the same behaviour and other behaviours as specificity controls; (3) direction = paired mean shift, tested for sufficiency (add to base) and necessity (remove from fine-tuned) by cross-model patching at several layers and at response positions; (4) outcome = judged behaviour on generated text with the DSSE rubric against base rate and random-fine-tune rate; (5) SAE validity re-measured on fine-tuned activations, including the share of the fine-tune shift that the reconstruction captures and feature displacements that keep the error term.

design_issues.why: Section H reports 0.91 for the correlation of variant-type means (about 35 heterogeneous groups from 'orig' to full swap) but 0.35 at the level of single states; the lens reproduces -0.26, 1.19, -0.18, 0.55, 0.90, 1.46, 1.39, 0.44 of the real output gap per pair and only 0.67 cosine with the stored final states (it was fitted on wikitext, not on chat-template positions).
design_issues.suggestion: Report within-variant-type and within-pair correlations with a calibration slope; do not use the lens direction as a reference for 'what the network reads' in pairs where the lens gap has the wrong sign.

design_issues.issue: Observational complement that needs neither synthetic states nor patching.
design_issues.why: Within-family natural variation on real held-out prompts already shows the pattern the patching finds (class-mean coordinate positively related to the output, probe-specific coordinate a suppressor) and is available for all 153 pairs and any number of splits at no forward-pass cost.
design_issues.suggestion: Add it as a standing section: within-family partial association of output measures with (a) probe coordinate, (b) class-mean coordinate, (c) their orthogonal remainder, plus the output shift of naturally misread prompts.

summary:
Verdict: the experiment is well instrumented (held-out references, random and random-label controls, swap, dose series, self-checks in the patching), but as designed it cannot answer "does separability by a probe tell us what the network uses", and several of its tables would be misread. The patched runs finished during the review; my recomputation reproduces the official numbers and shows what they actually support.

What the data support, for these 8 pair instances at split seed 0, block 21, last prompt token, first response token:
- The site is causally sufficient for the first-token family difference: full swap dR 1.11 (0.94-1.37 by pair).
- Moves along the hard-margin probe normal are direction-specific: +0.36 of the real gap over random or random-label directions of equal length (8/8 pairs, but not distinguishable from 0 inside pairs 3 and 5).
- At equal probe score the class-mean translation moves the output 2.4 times more (0.90 vs 0.38). This is fully explained by class-mean content: at s* the probe-normal state carries 0.44 of the class-mean difference, the translation 0.91. At equal class-mean coordinate the two lines agree at every dose (differences -0.06 to +0.02); at equal distance the ratio is 0.71. The honest reading is "the probe score overstates the B content of a minimum-norm move about twofold; the probe-specific remainder is causally inert", not "the network does not use what the probe separates".

What they do not support:
- General statements about probes: a C=1 SVM or a class-mean probe of the same accuracy has a normal with cosine 0.95-1.0 to the mean difference; the same attack states are read as B by 29% to 99% of alternative readouts.
- "Mimicry / high-density states are realistic B states": with this bandwidth the density term is a straight pull to the B centroid (kernel weights uniform, gradient cosine 0.999); lambda=5 and lambda=inf states are prototypes that no real state resembles, and they over-drive the output (1.30 vs 1.11 for a real swap in pairs 3-7).
- "The SAE reads the attack differently from the probe": a nearest-centroid rule on the raw state gives the same 0.30; the SAE drops more at this position (error norm 444) than the attack adds (307) and sees 8% of the probe-normal displacement.
- The density percentile, neighbour vote and isolation ratio as evidence of realism (real A states sit at the 20th percentile of B's density, the centroid at the 100th).
- The 8-pair means of dR: in pairs 0-2 both families start with "The", the real gap is 0.6-0.9 with intervals reaching almost 0 and AUROC 0.65-0.82; pair 7 is trivially separable. The informative pairs 3-6 give 0.06, 0.24, 0.03, 0.31 for the probe normal.
- dR2 as "the network's reaction": about a third to two fifths of it is the patched vector riding the residual connection.
- The printed intervals as generalisation: they resample sources only; between-split SD is 3.4 times the bootstrap SE where it can be checked, pair-level intervals are 2-4 times wider, the 8 pairs form 4 dependent clusters and were drawn mostly from the least separable family pairs.
- Rows sae5/sae20 (0 and 24 of 236 states valid; the "+1.66 [1.41,1.93] (3/3 pairs)" contrast is an artefact).
- Anything about DSSE side effects: the classes are base-model prompt families, not fine-tuned behaviours.

What must change before interpretation: (1) report equal-score, equal-distance and equal-class-mean matchings together and add the two dissociation variants (pure probe-specific move; probe-blind class-mean move); (2) repeat the closed-form attack for regularised and class-mean probes or scope the claim to the max-margin normal; (3) rename and reframe the large-lambda arm and replace the density/neighbour diagnostics by a discriminative side coordinate plus two-sided typicality; (4) gate the output measure per pair, propagate the denominator, use calibrated evasion at fixed false-positive rate, report per pair; (5) net the direct path out of dR2; (6) print the raw-state centroid readout beside every SAE reading and drop sae5/sae20; (7) common-support tables with counts; (8) at least 5 splits, more and randomly chosen pairs, hierarchical uncertainty, pre-specified primary contrasts.

Limits of this review: no forward passes of my own, one split for everything that involves the network, the matched-coordinate result relies on linear interpolation along a three-point class-mean line, and the pass-through share is calibrated on the random-direction controls rather than measured from the pre-norm state.
